verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both renders and the markdown bytes. PDF page 1014 (printed page 984), rendered at 300 dpi: the last content on the page is the two-line entry 'Javanese:' / 'A984-A9B2', followed by the folio '984 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license footer. There is NO 'Kaithi:' token anywhere on printed page 984 - I read the full page and enumerated every entry (1FD6-1FDB..., Gujarati, Gunjala_Gondi, Gurmukhi, Han, Hangul, Hanifi_Rohingya, Hanunoo, Hatran, Hebrew, Hiragana, Imperial_Aramaic, Inscriptional_Pahlavi, Inscriptional_Parthian, Javanese). PDF page 1015 (printed page 985) opens with 'Kaithi:' on its own line, then '11083-110AF', then 'Kannada:'. Markdown, verified byte-exact with `cat -A` at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:40401-40410: Javanese:$ A984-A9B2 Kaithi:$ $ $ ## Page 1015$ # ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)$ $ 11083-110AF$ Both halves of the claim quote their source accurately; neither is misquoted. I actively tried to refute this three ways and each attempt failed: (1) 'The text is present, just reflowed.' The token 'Kaithi:' is indeed still present and still precedes its range in reading order, so nothing is lost outright. But it has crossed an entry boundary: it now sits on the SAME physical line as the Javanese code-point ranges, with no separator other than a space. This whole section is a strict two-line record format - script name with trailing colon alone on one line, code-point ranges on the following line(s). Every one of the ~30 entries on pages 984-985 obeys that pattern; this is the single place in the region where it is broken. A line-oriented reader or extractor parses the Javanese entry's range list as 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:' (polluted with a stray non-range token) and then encounters '11083-110AF' as a range line with no owning script name. That is a changed name-to-range binding, i.e. content, not presentation. (2) 'It is only page-break furniture.' Furniture would be a running header, folio, or license line appearing or vanishing. Here a substantive data label migrated backward across the page boundary and fused to a different entry's data line. The furniture (anchor, '## Page 1015', running header) is intact and correct; the defect is separate from it. (3) 'Line wrapping / hyphenation.' No wrap is involved - the PDF has a hard paragraph break and a page break between 'A984-A9B2' and 'Kaithi:', not a soft wrap. One wording correction to the claim: the Kaithi range is not strictly 'unlabelled' in the sense of the label being deleted - the label survives, misplaced onto the preceding line on the previous page. The defect is a detachment plus line-merge, not a deletion. That refinement does not change the verdict.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with one wording refinement. At the boundary between printed pages 984 and 985, the PDF has 'Javanese:' / 'A984-A9B2' as the final entry of page 984, and 'Kaithi:' / '11083-110AF' as the first entry of page 985. The markdown pulls the 'Kaithi:' label backward across the page break and merges it onto the end of the Javanese range line, producing 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:' as a single line, and leaves '11083-110AF' at the top of page 1015 with no preceding script name on its own line. The label is not deleted - it is detached from its range and fused to the previous entry's data line - so two records are corrupted rather than one: the Javanese range list gains a spurious trailing token, and the Kaithi range loses its line-adjacent label. This breaks the section's uniform two-line 'ScriptName:' / 'ranges' record structure, which every other entry on pages 984-985 follows, and would mis-bind both entries under any line-oriented extraction of the Unicode script-to-code-point-range table.
